bib.title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters", Borui Kang, Jinrui Gu, Junhan Lv, Wenbin Li, Lei Wang, Yang Gao (Nanjing Univ.; Univ. of Wollongong). Venue: "Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027", so a preprint, not published. arXiv:2608.19013v2 [cs.LG], 30 Sep 2026. The ID implies v1 was in Aug 2026 (the text gives no v1 date). First author Kang, 2026.
COVERAGE: All 20 of 20 pages and 70,523 of 70,523 chars, including appendices A-G. The reference list was skimmed only. I did not run the figure-caption script. Captions are from the extracted text. Page numbers are approximate.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Defines Harness Continual Learning (HCL): a frozen model with an evolving harness H=(Interface I, Memory M, Capability Map C, Router R). Harness-level forgetting is a harness update that breaks previously reliable behaviour (a correct answer, a valid tool call, a successful trajectory) with no change to the model.
  number: none
  setup: Conceptual framing. Eq. 4 is H_n=(I_n,M_n,C_n,R_n). The four components are "jointly versioned".
  quote: "a memory update can change evidence retrieved for an earlier query, a skill revision can alter tool use, and a routing edit can break a previously successful workflow."
  where: p2, Intro
- Guarded evolution separates proposing from committing. An Optimizer proposes a candidate harness. An Evaluator commits it only if (i) current-task gain >= delta, (ii) historical loss <= budget B, (iii) it is valid. Otherwise the deployed harness is unchanged. The deployed harness is never modified during the search.
  number: none (gate is Eq. 10)
  setup: Historical loss D_n counts anchors the current harness solves that the candidate fails. Anchors are an evaluation-only set that execution and candidate generation never see. An LLM selector picks anchors, prioritising failures, format violations and brittle cases. Anchors are fixed while the next task is optimised.
  quote: "a candidate is admissible only if it (i) improves current-task performance by at least δn, (ii) keeps historical regression on the sampled anchors within Bn, and (iii) satisfies task-specific validity requirements."
  where: p6; anchors in App. B.1 (p15)
- On ALFWorld, Plasticity-HCL scores highest but forgets more. Stability-HCL scores nearly as high with much less forgetting.
  number: 62.98% final avg and 10.94% forgetting (Plasticity); 61.74% and 2.64% (Stability); best non-HCL baseline 55.56% (RAG)
  setup: Frozen Qwen3.5-9B, 6 sequential categories, 10 training episodes per category, 134 eval episodes. Baselines are Static Harness (47.12), RAG, MemP and MemRL (60.68, 1.76 forgetting), reimplemented in the same framework. For ALFWorld and Minecraft, strict historical backtesting is replaced by LLM-judged acceptance, because replay changes environment state.
  quote: "Plasticity-HCL obtains the highest final average success of 62.98%, compared with 55.56% for the best non-HCL baseline, but incurs 10.94% average forgetting. Stability-HCL achieves a comparable 61.74% final average while reducing average forgetting to 2.64%."
  where: p7, Table 1
  Note: MemRL (60.68, 1.76) is close to Stability-HCL on both. The Static Harness is not an evolving-harness baseline.
- Budget sweep: a small tolerance beats strict zero tolerance. Past that, accuracy and retention both worsen.
  number: b=0: 61.25 avg, 0.39% fgt; b=1: 63.46, 1.22%; b=3: 62.04, 2.00%; b=inf: 60.13, 3.45%
  setup: Frozen DeepSeek-V4-Flash, textual stream. 300 adaptation, 80 validation, 600 test examples per task. 80 anchors per earlier task. 40 proposal opportunities, delta of +2 validation cases, >=90% format compliance. Only b varies.
  quote: "b= 0 yields the lowest average forgetting of 0.39%, whereas b= 1 achieves the highest final average accuracy of 63.46%, improving over b= 0 by 2.21 percentage points with average forgetting of 1.22%."
  where: p8, Table 3
- Stronger model proposes, weaker model runs. A 27B model used only to generate candidate harnesses lifts a 4B executor with no latency cost. Using the 27B online costs about 4x the latency.
  number: Base 35.10% -> Opt-HCL 45.75% (+10.65 pp); latency 9.95 -> 9.72 s/sample; Online-HCL 44.80% at 39.31 s/sample
  setup: Qwen3-4B executor; Qwen3.6-27B as optimizer. All variants use Stability (B=0) on the four-task stream.
  quote: "Opt-HCL achieves a final average accuracy of 45.75%, improving over Base-HCL (35.10%) by 10.65 percentage points while maintaining comparable online latency (9.72 vs. 9.95 seconds per sample)."
  where: p9, Fig. 4
- Textual stream (MuSiQue, ProofWriter, GSM8K, HotpotQA): HCL beats the memory baselines.
  number: Plasticity 76.10 avg, 0.40% fgt; Stability 70.65, 0.27; MemRL 68.85, 0.07; MemP 65.45, 0.47; zero-shot 63.65
  setup: Frozen DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, thinking off, temperature 0. 250 adaptation, 50 validation, 500 test examples per task. GSM8K goes to 96.00 under Plasticity, which drives most of the gap.
  quote: "Plasticity-HCL achieves the highest final average of 76.10% with 0.40% average forgetting, while Stability-HCL ranks second with a final average of 70.65%."
  where: p8, Table 2
- The same stream on a different backbone gives a different trade-off, so the outcome is backbone-dependent.
  number: Plasticity 66.15% with 7.87% fgt; Stability 62.00% with 1.27%. MemP 62.55%, MemRL 62.20%, zero-shot 62.00%.
  setup: Frozen Qwen3.6-27B, same data budget and order. Stability-HCL ties zero-shot on average.
  quote: "This separate result indicates that the realized stability–plasticity outcome depends on the frozen backbone and optimization trajectory, even when the data budget and task order are matched."
  where: p17, Table 5
- Multimodal stream (COCO detection, caption, RefCOCO grounding, VQAv2): Stability-HCL has the best mean and low forgetting.
  number: Stability 68.92, 0.22% fgt; Plasticity 67.96, 0.81%; MemP 65.16 and MemRL 64.75 (both 0.00 fgt); zero-shot 46.77
  setup: Frozen Qwen3.6-27B, 250/50/500 split per task. Baselines forget nothing but gain less. Zero-shot beats every method on VQAv2 (85.47 vs <=79.80).
  quote: "Stability-HCL achieves the best final mean of 68.92 with only 0.22% average forgetting, while Plasticity-HCL reaches 67.96 with 0.81% forgetting."
  where: p8, Table 2
- Component ablation: freezing memory hurts most. Freezing the Capability Map hurts least.
  number: Full 63.41 avg, 0.45% fgt; w/o Interface 62.37; w/o Memory 62.28 with 0.83% fgt; w/o Capability 63.12; w/o Router 62.77
  setup: Frozen Qwen3.5-4B, multimodal stream, Plasticity profile. A frozen component stays available with its initial contents. Gaps are about 0.3-1.1 points, single run, no variance reported. Disabling memory also removes the source of new skills.
  quote: "Fixing Memory causes the largest performance drop and increases average forgetting to 0.83%. Some restricted variants exhibit lower forgetting because they also acquire less new capability."
  where: p9, Table 4; App. F, pp19-20
- Minecraft: HCL completes the whole curriculum while the static harness plateaus.
  number: 50 of 50 tasks vs 15 for the static harness; 83 cumulative actions vs 88 (MemRL) and 91 (MemP)
  setup: deepseek-v4-flash-0731, 50-task curriculum, Plasticity-HCL. Retained skill tests serve as anchors. Completed tasks are not systematically replayed, so forgetting is not measured here.
  quote: "Plasticity-HCL completes all 50 tasks, while the Static Harness plateaus at 15."
  where: p7, Fig. 3
- Exploratory: registering a calculator in the Capability Map lifts GSM8K. It is not causal.
  number: GSM8K 53.20% -> 90.40% (+37.20 pp); 254 of 500 examples routed to the calculator
  setup: Frozen Qwen3.6-27B. The comparison is against an earlier Stability-HCL run that also differed in prompts, retries and memory trajectories.
  quote: "Because the compared runs also differ in prompts, retries, and memory trajectories, these changes do not isolate the causal contribution of tool execution alone."
  where: p18, App. E, Fig. 6
- Optimizer procedure (App. B.2): sequential component-wise search. Components are taken in a fixed order. Up to K alternatives are generated per artifact, each tested by swapping only that artifact. The best admissible one is persisted before the next artifact is generated. If none passes, the artifact is unchanged. Memory and skill writes are first gated jointly as one implicit update and rolled back if rejected.
  number: none
  quote: "Among the admissible candidates, the Evaluator prioritizes current-task performance and uses lower anchor loss as the first tie-breaker. If no candidate is admissible, the artifact remains unchanged."
  where: p15, Algorithm 1

LIMITS
- Anchors are a sample, so b=0 does not guarantee zero test forgetting. The paper concedes this.
  quote: "The budget constrains regression on sampled anchors rather than all historical test cases, so b= 0 does not guarantee zero test-set forgetting."
  where: p8
- There is no limitations section. Nothing is reported on seeds, variance or significance. Gaps between variants are small.
- Baselines are only MemP, MemRL, RAG and a static harness, all reimplemented by the authors. It does not compare against other prompt-evolution or skill-evolution loops.
- The abstract's "relative gains exceeding 10%" holds only "in multiple settings". Gains are large on GSM8K, and the multimodal VQAv2 score falls below zero-shot.
- The paper shows no tests of semantic drift beyond anchors, no cost accounting for the optimizer calls, and no live deployment.
- Models are very recent and named inconsistently (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, V4-Flash and v4-flash-0731 are all used). The model names will date quickly.
- Plasticity-HCL's high-forgetting numbers (10.94 on ALFWorld, 7.87 on Qwen textual) show the unguarded variant forgets. The paper does not report a no-gate baseline in the same structure beyond b=inf.

BUILDS ON
- Classical continual learning: Delange et al. 2022 (survey), Kirkpatrick et al. 2017 (EWC), Lopez-Paz & Ranzato 2017 (GEM).
- Memory baselines: MemP (Fang et al. 2026), MemRL (Zhang et al. 2026c), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), MemGPT (Packer et al. 2023), Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023).
- Harness and agent loops: He et al. 2026, Li et al. 2026, Chen et al. 2026b (HarnessX), Gu 2026, Voyager (Wang et al. 2024a), Zhou et al. 2023 (APE).
- Lin et al. 2026, "Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit". Cited as support that repeated improvement alone gives no retention criterion.
- Benchmarks: ALFWorld (Shridhar et al. 2021), MuSiQue, ProofWriter, GSM8K, HotpotQA.

CODE (verbatim)
- Commit gate, Eq. 10 (p6): G(k)n = 1[ ∆(k)n ≥ δn ∧ D(k)n ≤ Bn ∧ vn(H̃(k)n+1) = 1 ]
- Deployment rule, Eq. 3 (p5): Hn+1 = H̃n+1 if Gn = 1, else Hn
- Historical loss, Eq. 9 (p5): Dn = Σ_{a∈An} 1[ q(Hn,a)=1 ∧ q(H̃n+1,a)=0 ]
- Forgetting, Eq. 11 (p17): Fgt_T = 1/(T−1) Σ_{j=1}^{T−1} ( max_{r∈{j..T}} R_{r,j} − R_{T,j} )
- Algorithm 1 loop (p15): for c in C' in configured order; evaluate each candidate q by replacing only H[c]; keep Q_ok where GATE=1; H[c] <- best; PERSIST before the next artifact.

FIGURES
- Fig. 1, p2: model-centric versus harness-centric continual learning. It shows that the learning object moves to the harness and a candidate is validated before it is accepted or rejected.
- Fig. 2, p4: HCL architecture. It shows the four components, Optimizer, Evaluator, and the separation of candidate harness from current harness state. Best figure for the four-component and gate picture.
- Fig. 3, p7: Minecraft cumulative tasks (50 vs 15) and cumulative actions (83/88/91).
- Fig. 4, p9: placement of the stronger model. Latency 9.95/9.72/39.31 s and accuracy 35.10/45.75/44.80.
- Fig. 5, p18: stage-wise forgetting by tolerance b (0.39 / 1.22 / 2.00 / 3.45). The panel labels are duplicated in the extraction.
- Fig. 6, p19: calculator ablation, with GSM8K +37.20 pp and 254/500 examples routed.

PROBLEMS: The extraction is clean, apart from garbled math and subscripts and duplicated panel labels in Fig. 5. There were no embedded instructions in the PDF. Table 1 bold and underline markers were lost, so rankings in the columns are inferred from the numbers. The Table 4 and Table 7 Zero-shot values differ in column detail, but the averages match (34.84). Table 7 shows zero-shot grounding as 0.00, while Table 2 (Qwen3.6-27B) shows 43.00. These are different backbones (Qwen3.5-4B versus Qwen3.6-27B). I did not run the figure-caption script.
